A Return Visit After Seven Years – Still as Enjoyable
Oct 2026 • Couples
This was my second visit to Vietnam House, my first being seven years ago. It’s heartening to see how well the restaurant has done over the years, with a second outlet now operating not far away.
The restaurant itself is beautiful, with an elegant, cosmopolitan ambience that makes for a lovely dining experience. Service was polished and professional, very much in keeping with the upmarket setting.
We ordered three savoury dishes and a dessert.
We started with the vegetarian rice spring rolls. As I’ve been gravitating towards a more plant-based diet, this was a natural choice. They were very good, and I certainly didn’t feel that anything was missing without the usual meat filling.
The highlight for me was the grouper fillet grilled in banana leaf. The fish was nicely charred and complemented by an excellent XO sauce that brought out its flavours beautifully.
The river prawns, unfortunately, were somewhat disappointing. At approximately S$40 for two large prawns, expectations were understandably high. While the dish was perfectly acceptable, I found it rather average and had expected something more memorable at that price point.
We rounded off the meal with a coconut-based dessert, which I believe was an off-menu offering. It was a lovely way to finish the meal and something I thoroughly enjoyed.
Overall, Vietnam House remains a very good restaurant, combining refined Vietnamese cuisine with an elegant setting and polished service. Despite the slight disappointment with the river prawns, I enjoyed this visit just as much as my first one seven years ago. It’s reassuring to see a restaurant maintain its standards over time, and I would certainly recommend it.

reviews.review_text:
UkVenturer
uk17 contributions

Nothing special.
Nov 2025 • Couples
Visited twice during our stay. Both times given a table upstairs, despite tables being free downstairs. First visit was reasonably ok. The food was tasty and well cooked, but no better than we had already experienced in most restaurants we used in Saigon. Nothing was exceptional here in our opinion. Wine list was extensive and we managed to choose one of our favourites. Service was just standard. Total cost just over 7 million Dong.
Second visit, was a disappointment however. Again, we were placed upstairs. Service was not great this time. Our starters were mixed up, the main course was just standard again and service was slow. This time we cut our meal short after a coach party of super load Americans turned up and were then seated at a long table near where we were seated. ( approx. 30). The ambience soon rapidly deteriorated .You couldn’t hear each other speaking, let alone the waiters. It turned into who can talk loudest competition at their table, not unlike rush hour at a fast food venue and was so unpleasant, we paid up and left. Just over 5 Million dong lighter in the Wallet. Sadly a couple of very pleasant Ladies, seated next to ourselves, also indicated that they too were going to leave. Again, there were empty tables downstairs. Overall, we were very disappointed. There are so many great restaurants available in HCMC, with great up and coming Chefs, that we cannot recommend this, unless the ambience described above suits your style. Sadly, it’s not our style. Eating should be more refined. Try Blanc de Blanc for example, superb food and incredible staff. A little more expensive, but well worth every penny. Also any of the restaurants in the Sofitel, Sheraton, Caravelle or many of the small independent ones. Over the two months we’ve spent dining out in Vietnam, we’ve done so many. If your budget is smaller, then equally great food at a fraction of the price can be found at Le Comptoir or Saigon Home for example. All were used by us along with many others.

Traditional Vietnamese Food, With A Modern Twist, In Elegant Surroundings
Jan 2025 • Couples
After discovering this gem a couple of years ago, we couldn’t wait to return—and we were pleased we did. 

Housed in a beautifully restored colonial building that once served as the iconic Café L’Imperial in the early 1900s, Vietnam House is a blend of historic charm and modern sophistication. The ambiance is warm and elegant, making it perfect for a special evening out.

The menu features traditional Vietnamese cuisine with a modern twist, crafted with precision and care. Since we’d had a large lunch, we kept it light with a starter and main:

 • Pork and Prawn Fresh Rolls: Fresh rice paper rolls filled with tiger prawns, pork, noodles, and herbs, served with a soy peanut sauce. A refreshing and flavorful start to the meal.
 • Twice Cooked Duck Breast with Plum Sauce: Perfectly pink duck breast with a rich plum sauce, paired with bok choy and creamy mashed potatoes. The dish was perfectly balanced and absolutely delicious.

The service was very good, with our server being attentive, knowledgeable, and friendly throughout the evening. It added a personal touch to an already lovely experience.

If you’re in Ho Chi Minh City and looking for an elegant dining experience, this Michelin-recognized spot is a must-visit.

Attentive manager and servers, beautiful decor, mod-Viet cuisine
Nov 2024 • Family
Wanted to find a restaurant which was:
(1) beautiful, cultural and hopefully in town
(2) variety and classy presentation of Vietnamese food
(3) wheelchair accessibility (including clean wheelchair toilets)
(4) vegetarian menu
(5) great service with initiative and understanding

It's quite rare, but Vietnam House managed to fulfil the above.

It's gorgeous at first glance, and the Art Deco features were befitting of this historical building of that colonial era. They're doing mod-Viet cuisines, which might not delight the purists or those who prefer full-on authentic flavours, but it might be easier on the palate for those who find it hard to venture to new flavours. Its proximity (just a few hundred meters away) to Nguyen Hue and L'hôtel de ville (Municipal Hall) meant it's still a manageable distance for our elderly guests to walk over and see one of the main and most beautiful streets of the city.

After we did our lunch reconnaissance of suitability for our wheelchair-bound guest, we requested the table with the arched stained glass backdrop, but the maitre d was more thoughtful by suggesting a table closer to the washroom - which indeed proved to be more convenient. During dinner with our guests, the manager and servers were attentive to our needs, observing and then taking initiative to help e.g. providing napkins for our overly hot teapot handles, communicating with us which dishes are suitable for the vegetarians among us, etc.

An overall wonderful and inclusive experience.

Very disappointing and flavorless experience
Oct 2023 • Couples
Hugely disappointing food experience. 

The team were nice and professional, the space was good but the food was the blandest food we have experienced in Vietnam. Our experience throughout the country has been one of highly flavored food. Tonight had none of that, our expectation was this would be sophisticated and high quality dining which we would happily have paid appropriately for. 

Between us we ordered lemongrass Iberico pork, soft shell crab, chicken and pork dishes as mains but we barely wanted to eat it as the food to us seemed totally tasteless. 

We gave feedback to the waitress when asked and said that the food was well below our expectations, she was good and understood we were very disappointed. She offered us tea and a complimentary desert which was appreciated but the reality was our experience didn’t live up to any of the excellent reviews.

Lesson for us is when the restaurant is so clearly catering for tourists be aware that a nice shiny restaurant and professional servers doesn’t make up for very average and relatively very expensive food. 

Big shame as we had been really looking forward to a sophisticated and flavoursome meal.

We were so excited to visit this restaurant. We love Vietnamese food and are familiar with many Vietnamese dishes. Booked weeks ahead to ensure our reservation. Service was first class. Restaurant ambience was very nice. Wine was very very expensive, but that's Vietnam, I guess. 

BUT the disappointing thing was the food. The fried squid was well executed, although fried in batter, which the wait staff said was not the case. The lobster netted spring rolls were very good.
 However as for everything else we ordered, we have had much tastier, more generous dishes in Australian restaurants serving Vietnamese food. The Vietnamese pancake (crab and iberico pork), a dish we love and have eaten in Vietnam and Australia was, quite frankly, more than disappointing. The crab was non- existent except for the orange coloured bits of unidentified chewy particles (resembling over-cooked egg yolk) which I suspect were supposed to be crab. I note that there were a few small prawns included (not on the menu) with which the chef was possibly hoping to bulk up the crab? Iberico pork? Well, rubbery bits of pork meat ( like dry pork mince). I must say, though, the generous and varied accompanying herbs were lovely and almost need a review of their own.

The La Vong Fish appertiser had no hint of dill and was a most poorly executed and dry dish, not anything like the famous Cha ca la vong dish of Han Oi which the chef was obviously hoping to identify it with.

Definitely dine at Vietnam House.
Jun 2023 • Couples
We dined at Vietnam House as a bit of special meal during recent trip to Vietnam. Vietnam is a country of amazing food, most that doesn’t cost a lot, and can be found in market stalls or low key restaurants, so splashing out on this meal was definitely a luxury! However, it was so worth it and an awesome experience. 

Husband and I are big fans of Luke Nguyen’s cooking and cooking shows, so when we learned he had a restaurant in Ho Chi Minh we knew we had to give it a go. The restaurant is on busy corner in District One in a beautiful old building. The decor is stunning - lots of glass, peacock blues, plush fabrics, and seating is designed so that it feels both comfortable but intimate. We sat upstairs, and though it was a rainy night, our table was near the balcony and gave a great view to the action of the street outside. Staff are attentive without being overbearing. 

We opted for the chefs selection set menu. There was a fantastic selection of dishes, and I love not having to pick but trusting that the dishes presented offer a taste of what the chef has to offer, as well as showcasing flavours and produce. Each dish was beautifully presented and delicious. I couldn’t list them all, so check out the pics below. We left feeling satisfied but not overly full, which is nice (there’s nothing worse than feeling food coma-ish after a meal) and I think it shows quality rather quantity is key here. 

It was an expensive night as far as eating in Vietnam goes, but by usual Australian standards, it wasn’t too crazy and I certainly think it was worth the money. 

Thanks to the team at Vietnam House for a fabulous foodie night and a great dining memory

Great decision to stop and dine at Vietnam House
Dec 2019
I dinned at Vietnam House for dinner 1 night on my tour of Vietnam. The staff was most welcoming. The ambience of the dining room was traditional Vietnamese with lots of wood and accents. I wanted to order almost everything on the menu. My waitress, Quynh, was most helpful in recommending some appetizers for me. The menu was in English however I could not decide on my own what to order. She recommended the shrimp mousse grilled on sugar cane and the traditional fried pork springs rolls. Both were delicious however the shrimp mousse was forever memorable. When my food arrived Quynh was most helpful in showing me how to prepare the shrimp mousse to so I enjoy all of the flavors that were presented on the plate. She prepared my first roll of the shrimp mouse in a leaf of lettuce with rice noodles, basil, mint, and sweet/sour fish sauce. The combination of the flavors was phenomenal. I savored each bite to the very end. Not every meal is memorable but this one certainly was. If you visit HCM you need to dine at Vietnam House. And be sure you ask for Quynh when you visit. She will ensure you will have a memorable experience as I did.

Hamish S
Wellington, New Zealand78 contributions

Service beyond reasonable expectation
Oct 2019
I was in Vietnam for the first time traveling for business and dined alone multiple times at Vietnam house during October 2019 after seeing Luke launch the restaurant on his show. 

Entering with high expectations, I traveled to Saigon specifically to eat at Vietnam house, believe it or not - the other things I did were simply biding time for the main event.

I dined the first time after reserving in advance (do so, it can be very busy during lunch and dinner hours especially) and ate their 3 course lunch special - it was very impressive and an introduction to some Vietnamese foods I had not tried before. I also tried their Cà phê trứng Việt Nam, Vietnamese egg coffee. It was simply exquisite.

What impressed me the most about the restaurant, was the level of service. The waiter, Mr. Tuong Pham was very considerate during the ordering process not only to explain any questions I had about the meals (mostly my interest in how it was made, not what it was) but also took the time to ask me about allergies, and checking with the chef to ensure that there were no dairy products in my food.

The second time I had Cà phê trứng Việt Nam again with seafood noodles and the bean curd pudding. The food again was simply so impressive, far beyond anything I could ever expect in my home country of New Zealand.

What impressed me the most was that on the second visit Mr Truong Pham again was my waiter and even though I am sure he had served so many since my visit two days earlier, he not only remembered me but remembered that I was lactose intolerant - and before accepting my order made sure with the chef that my order had no dairy.

I absolutely recommend the restaurant to anyone with specific dietary needs, anyone looking to treat themselves for something amazing (face it, you won't get anything near as good value in your home country) to visit the restaurant and enjoy the decor, the atmosphere, the food, and especially the service.

Sydney prices in HCMC. The place looks beautiful and the food was great. We paid about $100 per head. If you're looking for the cheaper set lunch then go on a weekday, not on a weekend. It's hidden deep in the fine print. The weekend lunch set is also not published on the website. There's 5% service charge and 10% tax added on top so factor that in as well as it wasn't clear on the website or menu. I would've enjoyed it more had the website not misled me into thinking this would be cheaper than a meal at home. I'm sure Luke pays his staff much less than George Calombaris. My fault for not having a keen eye for fine print, I was on holiday and didn't expect to have to read a menu as if it were a legal contract. The food though, was of excellent first world standard, I did love the egg coffee and I didn't get ill. Probably the best expensive Asian restaurant I've been to. I don't have a problem with the price, it's just the expectation set from what I read on the website. It's a really good display on the quality of food that Luke Nguyen does.

Minh L
Dear Agnes B,

First of all, thank you very much for taking the time to address your concerns in regards to your recent dining experience at Vietnam House restaurant. 

Glad you liked our ambiance, building decoration but its a shame to hear that you didn't like our 02 most popular dishes ( twice cooked duck breast and grilled chicken with wild pepper. Seems like a bit of an anomaly to me considering the feedback we received constantly praising our efforts. Our kitchen team has applied a new cooking method "sous vide" (Sous vide, which means “under vacuum” in French, refers to the process of vacuum-sealing food in a bag, then cooking it to a very precise temperature in a water bath) to most of the dishes with red meat and white meat in a la carte menu instead of using the traditional one( well cooked). The purpose is to keep the natural flavor and juices which are infused into the food while in the cooking pouch resulting in incomparable flavors and texture.
Actually, this cooking method is a little bit new to oriental culinary esp applied to Vietnamese local food and I think this is the main reason made you feel uncomfortable when seeing duck and chicken was a little bit pink in our food presentation. In reality, it is well-cooked already.

I am so sorry that the service crew has forgot to explain the food for you at your first uncomfortable feeling. If my service team informed you right away on that day, it might turn your observation on our food to a positive way. I wish if you informed us right away your feeling, the waitstaff surely explain clearly for you then bring it back to the kitchen for well cook as your eating habit .
I has conducted the training topic focusing on this issue for my team in order to prevent the same situation might cause in the future.

Thank you very much for your candid review and apologies once again.

Avoid if you like to laugh
Apr 2019 • Family
We had high expectations of the Vietnam House Restaurant as the interior was beautiful and the menu looked extremely tasty. Unfortunately our expectations were not met.....firstly, they tried to serve me a glass of champagne with no bubbles in it. Instead of bringing a fresh bottle they became quite indignant and said that it was the only bottle of champagne they had and it was either have it flat or not at all! Not a great start. The food was "ok" - not bad, but not nearly as tasty as the food we had eaten the night before in a restaurant which was charging half the price (Home Finest). We started with the prawns and scallop rolls which were a bit tasteless with overcooked prawns and the pork spring rolls which were nice. Then we has the cod, the chilli prawns, the 5 spice chicken and the wagyu beef cheeks stew. All of it was ok but nothing to write home about. We were about to sample the dessert menu when one of the waiters approached out table to tell us that we were being too loud and could we please be quiet as this was a refined establishment! I didn't know whether to laugh or cry to be honest. Our family of five (three children aged between 9 and 14) had been laughing and enjoying some good conversation - we are used to dining in fine restaurant all over the world, some of which with michelin stars and in all honesty we have never been told off for being too loud! The irony of the situation is that it was 8:30 in the evening and we were in an empty section of the restaurant so it wasn't like there were any other guests who could have been annoyed by a little laughter! My husband and I had consumed 2 small glasses of wine so it was hardly the case that we were unaware of our noise levels! Needless to say this reprimand killed the night dead and we opted to cut our evening short. Hugely disappointing but luckily as we are staying in the gorgeous Reverie Hotel just down the road so we were able to swoop back there for dessert! Thank goodness for restaurants and hotels that understand the importance of good customer service and don't mind families having a good time.

So if you wan a mediocre meal in a quiet environment with a hand break on happiness then I would definitely recommend this restaurant!

reviews.review_text:

Went for lunch... stayed for dinner...
Feb 2019 • Couples
After spending a couple weeks traveling throughout SEAsia, trying various street food and markets, we decided it was time to have a service led sit down meal. Looking for a place nearby our shopping circuit we decided on Vietnam House. We were delighted to see that not only were they open during Tet, but have a well designed website that was in itself interesting to navigate. Deciding on the lunch menu, we made our way there after some light shopping. 
Stepping in we were quickly greeted and led to a table with the general context of each menu being explained. Taking a quick look around you can tell some time has been spent in creating the decor and atmosphere, as it was quite pleasing to the eye and we didn't have the feeling of being on top of another table or vice versa. I didn't inquire about the upstairs seating, but I assume it is equally tasteful.
Perusing the menu, we noticed that we weren't given the lunch menu, being the reason of our visit. On asking about it we were told they weren't doing lunch that day. I can take it as Tet being a stress on a restaurant and only having to prepare one menu is easier. The dinner menu was nonetheless as pleasing as the lunch menu and we were satisfied with the selections. 
We ordered two starters and two entrees, plus a bottle of French sauvignon blanc which paired with our meal quite nicely. The food came out in a timely fashion and was quite delicious. The first course was a papaya salad. The portion was quite large and I would suggest sharing this dish. Honestly it's enough for four people but it didn't distract from the meal. Next we tried the lobster rolls. There were four to order and paired with lettuce to wrap and various herbs to add before applying a sweet/sour sauce. These were quite delicious and the texture of the rolls was a welcoming surprise. My only take away, the herbs could over power the rolls and the lobster was at times challenging to register. The entree course was excellent, choosing the filet of grouper with dragon beans and the duck served with bok choy and mashed potatoes. Both dishes were well received and quite the change of pace of our recent meals on holiday. The grouper was prepared well and cooked to near perfection. There was a slight crispiness to outer flesh but very moist throughout. The fish was well balanced with the rest of the plate. The duck was absolutely delightful. Not expecting to have mashed potatoes in Asia, it was quite a surprise to see it on the menu. The tomato sauce and bok choy on the plate made for a well balanced meal. The duck itself was prepared perfectly, with nice crispy, golden skin, full of flavor.
We thought about dessert but we were overly stuffed... perhaps too much papaya salad, and opted instead for a post meal coffee.
The service here was excellent. From the moment we walked in to the moment we left, we were constantly attended to but not leaving the feeling of being overshadowed. The waitress kept our glasses filled and the manager/maitre d' stopped by a couple times to inquire about our meal. Near the end of our meal we were also informed of the kitchen's closing time if we wanted to have anything else to finish off our meal before they shut down. That was nice to know if we decided to change our mind on dessert. Service time was prompt and timely, fitting that of a fine dining establishment.
Vietnam House was a good experience and we were overly satisfied with our choice in lunch for the day. Prices are higher when comparing to other local eateries, but I didn't feel at anytime I wasn't getting value for the money. Perhaps a sancerre on the menu would have been a better wine pairing, but that's just a preference.
Good eats!

Disgusted. After a month travelling through Vietnam, our final meal before flying home was to be a special.lunch at the restaurant of a celeb chef favourite of mine Vietnamese Aussie Luke Nguyen's branded Saigon House.
My girlfriend who is allergic to all seasfood, obviously not always easy to eat in Vietnam, but with warning our tours and other restaurants have mainly managed this request. Here however, after carefully scouring the menu and finding a duck dish that had absolutely no mention of seafood, we were informed it was injected with fish sauce and we should therefore try a vegetarian meal. Finding this exceptionally offensive we walked out, despite ordering wines and cocktails.
The menu clearly states to talk to the staff about allergies, which we did. If they cannot do a such of duck without fish sauce on request, it is quite obviously not prepared fresh.

Minh L
Dear chyciebabe,

First of all, I would like to thank for your visiting our restaurant on 31st of January,2019. Unluckily, we could not meet your girlfriend dietary requirement. She is allergic to all seafood.
As everybody know, to make Vietnamese food, most of ingredient is related to fish sauce and in Vietnam House restaurant, the fish sauce going with most of dishes in our a la carte menu.
In Vietnam House , 90% the food is prepared fresh. The others 10% we can not make fresh as you mentioned such as the Duck Breast, Five Spices Chicken, etc. . . Kitchen team need at least 05 minutes to marinate and 02 hours in the permeability.
About the menu wording, I think that most of the menu in the world, they could not write down 100% what in side in each dishes.
In Vietnam House restaurant, we do the same. But to ensure the guest having a safe food while they might forget to inform the wait staff their dietary requirement, the service crew is being trained an important task " how to address and recognize guest dietary requirement while taking order". The waiter served you on that day did his job very well as he did check and politely informed your girlfriend about fish sauce in her dish. He also suggested some dishes without fish sauce for you but unluckily, you refused. 
Moreover, if we make your Duck Breast without fish sauce ,you have to wait for it at least 1 hour and a haft, I think no one can wait such a long time for their dish at lunch.
Lastly, all Vietnam House team are very proud of our Master Chef Luke Nguyen as he made a great menu with lot of positive comments from others guests. I do apologize as our foods is not your flavor.
By the way, I would like to informed you that you had left the restaurant without paying your drinks while it was served in very good quality and politely way.
Hopefully you can find out suitable restaurants matching your requirement.

Beautiful setting ... unspectacular food

Australians who love their Vietnamese food and who follow "our" Luke Nguyen from the TV may be disappointed in this restaurant. The setting over two floors is stylish and classy but the food, I'm afraid, seems to have been designed for TV fans and European palates. 
There is so much good food in Vietnam - one of the cullinary hot spots on the planet - and so much good Vietnamese food in Australia that you have to wonder why Luke has pitched his dishes towards the bland end of the spectrum.
The answer, of course, is probably that American and Northern Europeans tend to be wary of highly spiced and strongly flavoured food and big ticket restaurants have to follow the money. 
It's a shame. We were hoping this would be one of the highlights of our tour but it turned out to be a low point - not that it was bad, just disappointing. Even our hotel concierge tried to steer us to a more authentic restaurant. But the decor is spectacular so maybe drop in for lunch.

reviews.review_text:

Mixed Feelings
Oct 2018 • Couples
My wife & I were very much looking forward to dining here on our last night in Vietnam. After discussing our thoughts about our dining experience we both agree we have mixed feelings about Vietnam House. 

Overall the ambience & decor was excellent, beautiful light installations that looked like large rain drops bouncing off the road after a large down pour - simply stunning!

The staff whilst were maybe a little too attentive, I would like to say Tuong was fantastic and very knowledgeable of the menu & Vietnamese food.

The cocktails and wine were good, priced as expected. The wine list is extensive, I was surprised not to see as many WA wines.

The food is where my wife and I had lengthy discussions and we both agree that whilst all dishes were tasty they missed the mark in terms of an upscale restaurant. We were not wowed by the food & have had tastier treats on the street!

I had the lobster rolls for entree, these were good, the dipping sauce was just missing some heat in the chilli. 

My wife had the pork ribs for entree & in her words the fermented pork we had in Hanoi at a Bia Hoi was tastier.

My dinner of the Garoupa in XO was delish, I just wished I had more of the XO!!

My wife’s beef cheeks - whilst promising to be tender - were hit and miss, she also hadn’t realised it was more of a hot pot, which she is generally not a fan of. She found the taste to be quite bland, she didn’t find the dish exciting.

We had a side of Thien Ly Flower - this was recommended by Tuong and this did not disappoint. 

If you go - remember to wear closed in shoes, we had read an earlier review and changed our footwear, I’m glad we did as when we arrived the waitress looked us both up & down - this was quite unnerving, nevertheless we got to experience one Luke Nguyen’s restaurants.

Smoked potato mash and smoking cocktail!
Sep 2018 • Couples
Have visited Vietnam house three times. First for dinner, then twice for lunch. Was difficult to choose, as so much looked good. And we were about to order maybe too much but the waiter advised what would be enough for two persons. And it was more than enough. All was good but the banh xeo and the smoked potato mash with the twice cooked duck breast really stood out. (However the mash was not mentioned for the duck in the menu but was a very tasty surprise, indeed). Regarding the banh xeo, the menu says "Crab & Iberico Pork". We found shrimps too. If that was because lack of crab meat available, I don't know. Anyway it tasted extremely good. Wish there was a set dinner menu for less than 4 persons too, as it might be a bit difficult to choose.

Second visit, we had the set lunch menu. I had the soft shell crab salad, Hoi An chicken rice and the bean curd for dessert. All good but the chicken was awesome! 

Third time there seemed to be only one set lunch menu available. Anyway, we just chose one dish each from the ala carte menu. Banh xeo with Iberico pork again and soft shell crab salad. All good, however the salad is not exactly overloaded with crabs...

Seems they have a weekly special cocktail in addition to others. Tried two; Gentleman with Jack Daniel's flavoured with smoked star anise and cinnamon stick. Fun and tasty effect! Second was a Tabasco mojito. Hot! They have different coffees on the menu, including civet coffee.

So is Vietnam House cheap? Of course not. But except for maybe just a couple of dishes I saw on the menu, I think it is quite reasonable for what you get. Very tasty food and drinks. And top notch service in a beautiful setting. 

Looking forward to visit again!

reviews.review_text:
shanthini41
Sydney, Australia105 contributions
1
Brash and buzzy
Sep 2018
Australian Luke Nyugen's Vietnam House restaurant in the very centre of busy Ho Chi Minh City is an assault on the senses with bold Art Deco interior design featuring vivid colours and a buzzy atmosphere. It feels exactly right where it is located in the heart of the CBD surrounded by the glitz of the high end designer shops like Louis Vuitton and Gucci and 5 star hotels. The menu features Nyugen's unique take on Vietnamese food that reflects the influences of growing up in Australia and his time spent in France through the use of imported herbs and ingredients, such as Wagyu beef, dill and salmon. We began with the much talked about soft spring rolls with sesame seared salmon and salmon caviar. The addition of the salmon caviar added delicious bursts of flavour to this entree and the flavour of the salmon went really well with the dill in the rolls. For mains we tried the much talked aboutBraised Wagyu Beef cheek in coconut juice, Phu Quoc green pepper, carrot, shallot served with Vietnamese baguette, and Grilled 5 spices free range chicken, fresh herbs, baby leek & thien ly flower. The baguette served with the Wagyu beef was perfect to mop up the delicious and almost delicate sauce with the beef. I thought the beef needed to be cooked slightly longer because it wasn't as tender as I would have expected and was still slightly chewy. The taste of the dish was very good and the carrots and potatoes stewed alongside the beef carried beautiful flavours. A side dish of vietnamese mint, lime and chillies gives diners the opportunity to add flavour to their taste. The free range grilled chicken was absolute perfection though, perfectly spiced and juicy with flavour. The thien ly fowers with baby leek were an ideal combination - these edible flowers are sweet and taste like crunchy peas and are traditionally served lightly stir-fried in Vietnam. Unfortunately we had no room to try dessert as much as I would have loved to try the Pandan Creme Brûlée or the Vietnamese Coffee Flan. Overall it was a lovely dinner with a few rough edges including rather run of the mill service. A proper welcome to the restaurant and an explanation of the food concept would help new visitors or those unaccustomed to Nyugen's style to better appreciate the menu. I would still rate the experience highly as 4/5 and would go back to try those desserts next time I'm in town.

reviews.review_text:
Warren H
Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam308 contributions
1
Appealing fusion Vietnamese right down town
Aug 2018 • Friends
Vietnam House, a creation of Luke Nguyen has emerged in an older French building in a premium location on Dong Khoi street. Lukes influence is evident immediately at entry with his cook books displayed prominently. The restaurant has been lovingly restored and is impressive inside including an ancient lift to the upper floors. With this location it is very accessible to tourists who I think would be the main customers. 
We took some overseas visitors there and our group of 4 enjoyed a wide range of dishes. Some dishes are very similar to traditional Vietnamese food such as the Shrimp Mousse Grilled On Sugar Cane, the ubiquitous Wok Tossed Morning Glory, Grilled 5 Spices Free Range Chicken and X.O. Garoupa Fillet Char Grilled in Banana Leaf. Other dishes were an interesting modern/fusion twist such as Prawn & Hokkaido Scallop Mustard Leaf Rolls, Deep Fried Chili Lemongrass Iberico Pork Ribs, Twice Cooked Duck Breast With A Tomato Pepper Sauce, Wok Tossed Cubed Pepper Beef Tenderloin with Smoked Potato Mash ( a twist on Bo Luc Lac). We didn't have a standout dish and enjoyed each and I think it is not competing directly with traditional Vietnamese food but adding another dimension.
Service was attentive and well paced, pricing is reasonable, food was nice and it is set in a lovely centrally located building. Would definitely recommend a visit alongside the traditional Vietnamese restaurants you should also eat at.

The restaurant is situated in the fashionable Dong Khoi street and very close to the Grand Saigon hotel. Reservation for dinner is a must to avoid disappointment.

Set in a beautiful building the restaurant has seating on two floors and there is a twee lift to the first floor. Pleasant decor using wood and marble. We found the ground floor a little noisy and asked to move upstairs where the boothed seating is more private. Vietnamese music in the background.

Interesting menu, set menu and a la carte available and vegetarians very well catered for.

The Mussel Bay white wine which was served with tasty sweet/chilli peanuts complimented our dishes. We opted for: soft crab and green mango salad - bursting with flavours, vegetarian netted spring rolls (wrapped in lettuce leaves and fresh herbs) - divine, vegetarian turmeric curry - subtle flavours, vegetable fried rice - lovely al dente vegetables, Vietnamese coffee flan and pandan creme brulee with coconut icecream/sesame tuile - divine! A disappointing experience
Feb 2018 • Family
We booked to come to Vietnam House following the trip advisor reviews and an article my mum had seen in the paper back home in the UK. 

The restaurant interior was lovely but unfortunately for us that was as good as it got which is a shame. 

There were 5 of us eating in total. 3 ordered starters of spring rolls / soup and fish wraps. For mains we went for 2 chicken breasts / duck / beef and pigeon. The waitress struggled to repeat back our order as she had written it across various blank spaces in her notepad so we weren't sure we would get what we ordered. We were told there could be a 30 minute wait for the food as it was made fresh which were we fine with and they checked if we wanted things to come as they were ready or in order of starters then mains, we said starters first then mains. It seemed a slightly strange question but went with it.

The first dish to arrive was the chicken breast then the duck then the three starters. We tried to explain that we had asked for things separately but they didn't really understand. The chicken was nice but aired as if it had been  ready for a while, similar for the duck. The spring rolls were lovely and very hot, straight from the oven. The fish wraps were bland and lacked any taste.

After we finished the remaining main courses arrived along with a side dish that should have come with the duck which didn't get eaten. The beef was cold which had to be sent back and was made again from scratch. The second chicken dish was also aired although cooked through. The pigeon was also aired.

We did ask to speak to the manager as we were extremely disappointed especially as there were some basic errors which shouldn't have occurred and we were expecting a lot more. He was extremely apologetic saying the restaurant had been busy but that it shouldn't be an excuse. We settled on a discounted bill as well as the offer to return another evening so they could show us how good it could be. Unfortunately we didn't have enough nights left in the city to do this. 

Hopefully the adjustments can be made and staff training tailored where needed so that they can learn where they can improve.
